description: Component-based UI from the ground up: JSX, props, component composition, and the mental model that underlies every React application.

lessons.title: Why React?
lessons.description: Understand the problem React solves: describing interfaces as reusable components whose rendered output changes when application state changes, instead of manually coordinating DOM updates throughout the application.
lessons.originalIntent: Understand the problem React solves: describing interfaces as reusable components whose rendered output changes when application state changes, instead of manually coordinating DOM updates throughout the application.

lessons.title: JSX
lessons.description: Learn JSX as the syntax React uses to describe UI, combine markup-like structure with JavaScript expressions, and practice the rules that make JSX different from ordinary HTML.
lessons.originalIntent: Learn JSX as the syntax React uses to describe UI, combine markup-like structure with JavaScript expressions, and practice the rules that make JSX different from ordinary HTML.

lessons.title: Components
lessons.description: Build reusable React components as focused functions that return JSX, and learn to break a growing interface into smaller pieces instead of putting everything inside one giant component.
lessons.originalIntent: Build reusable React components as focused functions that return JSX, and learn to break a growing interface into smaller pieces instead of putting everything inside one giant component.

lessons.title: Props
lessons.description: Learn how parent components pass read-only data into child components through props, and practice changing those inputs to see the child render different UI.
lessons.originalIntent: Learn how parent components pass read-only data into child components through props, and practice changing those inputs to see the child render different UI.

lessons.title: State
lessons.description: Learn how useState gives a React component local changing data, why updating state schedules a re-render, and why directly mutating state does not produce the intended React update.
lessons.originalIntent: Learn how useState gives a React component local changing data, why updating state schedules a re-render, and why directly mutating state does not produce the intended React update.

lessons.title: Conditional Rendering
lessons.description: Practice choosing between JSX branches with ternaries, logical &&, and early returns so components display the correct UI for their current state.
lessons.originalIntent: Practice choosing between JSX branches with ternaries, logical &&, and early returns so components display the correct UI for their current state.

lessons.title: Lists and Keys
lessons.description: Practice rendering arrays of data into JSX with map and learn why each rendered item needs a stable key that identifies the item across renders.
lessons.originalIntent: Practice rendering arrays of data into JSX with map and learn why each rendered item needs a stable key that identifies the item across renders.

lessons.title: React Mini Project
lessons.description: Build a small React application that combines components, props, state, conditional rendering, and lists into one coherent feature.
lessons.originalIntent: Build a small React application that combines components, props, state, conditional rendering, and lists into one coherent feature.
